terms.definition: The part of a plant that makes seeds, with petals and the stamen and pistil reproductive parts.
terms.function: Produces the seeds of the next plant generation.
terms.whereItIs: Growing on the stem, held up toward the light.
terms.whyItMatters: Flowers are how many plants make the seeds that grow into new plants.

terms.definition: The colored, often scented leaves around the flower that attract pollinators.
terms.function: Guides bees and birds to the flower so they can move pollen.
terms.whereItIs: The outer ring of a flower.
terms.whyItMatters: They let the flower recruit helpers to deliver pollen between flowers.

terms.definition: The male part of a flower that makes pollen at its tip.
terms.function: Produces and holds the pollen that plants need to make seeds.
terms.whereItIs: A ring of slender stalks around the center of the flower.
terms.whyItMatters: It makes the pollen that must reach a pistil for a seed to form.

terms.definition: The female part of a flower that receives pollen and is where a seed forms.
terms.function: Takes in the pollen and grows a seed in its base.
terms.whereItIs: The upright column at the center of the flower.
terms.whyItMatters: It is what must receive pollen for the flower to become a fruit with seeds.
